Keep the elbow lower than the wrist, and the shoulder heavy.

items.wl: Lu. Turn, sit back, lead the force past you.
items.go: From the bow stance, turn and sit back as the hands draw the arm past you.

c.l: Do not pull with the arms. Turn the waist and sit into the back leg.
Lead the force just past your body, not into it. A little more, and he falls forward.

items.wl: Ji. Two arms, one shape, driven by the legs.
items.go: Palm on the forearm. Drive from the back leg.

c.l: The arms do not extend. The whole body moves forward behind them.
Keep the shape round and compact, as if pressing a large ball against a wall.

items.wl: An. Sink, then drive from the back leg.
items.go: Sit back, palms down, then push from the ground.

c.l: The push begins in the back foot. If your arms push first, you have already lost.
Push slightly upward, to lift his root, not straight through him.

items.wl: Fa Jin Palm. Relax, explode, relax.
items.go: Relax first. Then release the palm in one sharp instant.

c.l: The explosion lasts a fraction of a second. Before and after, you are soft.
Snap the waist and the back heel at the same time. The palm is only the messenger.

items.wl: Hidden-Hand Punch. Coil, then uncoil.
items.go: Wide stance. Coil the waist, then fire.

c.l: The opposite elbow drives back as the fist drives forward. Two directions, double power.
Exhale sharply at the moment of the strike, then relax at once.

items.wl: Separate-Foot Kick. Cross, lift, snap.
items.go: Cross the wrists, lift the knee, and snap the kick out.

c.l: Lift the knee first, then extend. A kick without a chamber is only a swing.
Hands and foot open at the same moment.

items.wl: Snake to Rooster. Drop low, rise like a spring.
items.go: Sink as low as you can control, then rise and drive the knee.

c.l: Go only as low as you can rise from without using your hands.
The rise is one explosive motion: shift, stand, knee, palm.

items.wl: Single-Hand Push Hands. Stick and follow.
items.go: Bow stance, forearm forward. Draw the circle with your weight.

c.l: Sit back as the arm draws in, shift forward as it extends. The legs drive the circle.
Imagine a partner's arm. Never lose contact, never push against it.

items.wl: Dantian Breathing. Gather everything below the navel.
items.go: Palms on the belly. Breathe low and slow.

c.l: Breathe in through the nose and let the belly expand into your palms.
Breathe out slowly. Let the shoulders, the chest and the mind settle.

lines: The gauntlet. Tomorrow is your final test, so today we go hard.
Today's skill: Unshakable root.
Three minutes in the horse, the gates, the power strikes and the kicks, back to back.
You survived the gauntlet. Rest well. Tomorrow, the master's test.
Tomorrow: Tai Chi warrior.

items.wl: Rise and Sink. Legs and arms as one.
items.go: Your turn. Soft knees. Let the arms ride on the legs.

c.l: The legs lift the arms. The shoulders never do the work.
Sink a little deeper every time, and feel the thighs wake up.

items.wl: Double-Hand Silk Reeling. Two wheels, one engine.
items.go: Your turn. Sink, and let both hands begin to turn.

c.l: Never let the circles go flat. Up, out, down, in.
The knees stay over the toes while the waist turns. The hips do not wobble.

items.wl: Standing Post. Hug the tree. Be still.
items.go: Sink a little, round the arms, and hold.

c.l: Shoulders heavy, elbows heavy, the crown of the head floating up.
Your arms will want to drop. Keep them round, and breathe into the belly.
Five minutes. The master's stillness.

items.wl: Four-Gate Push Hands. Peng, Lu, Ji, An.
items.go: Begin with ward off and let the loop roll.

c.l: No corners between the gates. One flows into the next like water.
Ward off receives, roll back leads, press closes, push releases.

items.wl: Cai. Sharp, short, downward.
items.go: Grip, sink and pluck.

c.l: The pull is short and sudden. A long pull gives him time to recover.
Sink your weight at the moment of the pluck. The body drops, the hand follows.

items.wl: Lie. Opposite forces, one turn of the waist.
items.go: Turn the waist and split the arms apart.

c.l: One hand rises forward, one sinks back. Both are driven by the same turn.
Root the back foot. Splitting power without a root is only waving.

items.wl: Zhou. Step in, turn, strike.
items.go: Step in low and turn the whole body behind the elbow.

c.l: The support hand on the fist adds the second engine.
The elbow travels a short distance. All the power comes from the turn.

items.wl: Kao. Step deep, sink, burst.
items.go: Step in deep, sink low and strike with the shoulder.

c.l: The shoulder does not swing. The legs drive the whole torso forward as one block.
Guard your face with the other hand.

items.wl: Single Whip. Hook, step, strike.
items.go: Form the hook, step wide, and strike with the palm.

c.l: Hook and palm stretch apart like a bow being drawn.
The strike lands as the front foot settles. Hand and foot arrive together.

items.wl: Parry and Punch. Deflect, parry, strike.
items.go: Step, deflect, parry, punch.

c.l: The parry clears the line. The punch fills it. No pause between them.
Punch with a vertical fist at chest height, the shoulder relaxed.

items.wl: Heel Kick. Chamber, thrust, hold.
items.go: Knee high, then drive the heel forward.

c.l: Strike with the heel, toes pulled back. The heel carries the power.
The standing leg is rooted and slightly bent. The body leans neither forward nor back.

items.wl: Needle and Fan. Plunge, rise, thrust.
items.go: Sit back and plunge, then rise and thrust.

c.l: Fold from the hips, back long. The needle goes down, the eyes stay forward.
Rise and step in one motion. The front palm and front foot arrive together.

items.wl: Combat Flow. Parry, palm, elbow, shoulder.
items.go: Flow through the four techniques without a single pause.

c.l: Each technique steps closer. Hand range, elbow range, shoulder range.
No pause between strikes. Each one sets up the next.
Your final combat flow. Show me everything.

u.l: Tai Chi warrior. Thirty days, the eight gates, fa jin and the combat flow. You earned this.

items.wl: Dantian Breathing. Gather everything below the navel.
items.go: Palms on the belly. Breathe low and slow.

c.l: Breathe in through the nose and let the belly expand into your palms.
Breathe out slowly. Let the shoulders, the chest and the mind settle.

lines: Thirty days. This is the master's test.
Today's skill: Tai Chi warrior.
Five minutes of standing post, then everything you have learned, from the eight gates to the combat flow.
You are a Tai Chi warrior. Keep training, and this power will grow for the rest of your life.
Bow to your training. I will see you on the path.

plans.title: Shake, Tap & Wake
plans.subtitle: 8 min · Qigong self-massage wake-up
plans.description: Shake out from the knees, drum the thighs and lower back, swing from the waist, circle the hips and lift the sky. The quickest way to go from stiff to switched on.

plans.title: Daily Qi Awakening
plans.subtitle: 15 min · the first nine Shibashi forms
plans.description: The opening half of Shibashi — chest openings, the rainbow, rolling arms, rowing the boat and turning to the moon — closed with stillness.

plans.title: Shibashi 18
plans.subtitle: 18 days · one Qigong form a day
plans.description: Learn the 18 flowing forms of Tai Chi Qigong Shibashi progressively. Each lesson pairs a new form with earlier movements, with each video appearing only once. Days 6 and 12 bring the learned sections together, and day 18 flows through all eighteen forms in order.

items.g: Today, learn the opening and chest expansion separately. Keep the knees soft and the shoulders relaxed.
Today, paint the rainbow with an easy side reach. Let the waist move without forcing a stretch.
Today, separate the clouds with rounded arm paths. Keep the hands light as they rise and open.
Today, roll the arms smoothly from the shoulders. Avoid jerking the elbows or arching the back.
Today, row with an easy hinge and relaxed hands. Keep the range comfortable through the forward reach.

days.title: Lifting the Ball · the first seven forms

items.g: Today, bring the first seven forms together, with the ball lift as your new movement. Keep an even pace through each reset.

days.title: Turning to Gaze at the Moon

items.g: Today, turn to gaze at the moon with the waist. Let the head follow rather than twisting the neck alone.
Today, coordinate the waist turn and palm push. Keep your knees aligned as your torso turns.
Today, sway the arms from a comfortable horse stance. Keep the feet grounded without forcing the stance lower.

days.title: Scooping the Sea, Looking at the Sky

items.g: Today, scoop and rise through a comfortable range. Keep the neck relaxed as the gaze lifts.
Today, let the wave travel through a gentle weight shift. Keep the hands soft instead of pushing forcefully.
Today, bring the first thirteen forms together, with Flying Dove as your new movement. Keep the shoulders relaxed through the wings.
Today, punch with control from a steady stance. Do not snap the elbow or strike forcefully.
Today, let the goose wings rise without shrugging. Match the arm range to your shoulder comfort.
Today, trace the spinning wheel smoothly. Keep your balance as the arms travel around the body.
Today, coordinate the bouncing ball with a light step. Use a small lift rather than a forceful bounce.

days.title: Pressing Palms to Calm the Qi

items.g: Today, gather and press the palms gently. Let the breath stay natural as the hands lower.
Today, rehearse all eighteen Shibashi forms once. Choose a steady rhythm and finish without rushing.

plans.title: Eight Brocades Daily
plans.subtitle: 12 min · the complete Ba Duan Jin
plans.description: All eight brocades in one flowing practice — from Holding Up the Heavens to Bouncing on the Toes — for a full-body stretch and calm energy.

plans.title: Eight Brocades
plans.subtitle: 14 days · the classic Ba Duan Jin
plans.description: Learn Ba Duan Jin, the Eight Brocades, through progressive stretching, turning and strengthening lessons. Each video appears once per lesson, including both bow directions. Build towards the complete set with breath-led practice, controlled stance work and one sustained endurance session.

days.title: Standing like a tree · Hold Up the Heavens

items.g: Today, find a comfortable stance before lifting the hands. Learn the overhead path without locking the elbows.
Today, draw the bow in both directions. Keep the shoulders low and your knee following the foot.
Today, separate heaven and earth with opposing hands. Keep your torso tall instead of leaning into the reach.
Today, turn for Wise Owl within a comfortable range. Let the waist contribute without forcing the neck.

days.title: Sway the Head and Shake the Tail

items.g: Today, sway from the hips in a controlled stance. Choose a depth that lets you return upright smoothly.
Today, hinge comfortably towards the feet. Bend the knees if needed and rise without pulling on the back.

days.title: Recovery · the first six, slow and full

items.g: Today is a lighter Brocades practice. Use higher stances and smaller ranges through the first six movements.

days.title: Clench the Fists with Angry Eyes

items.g: Today, practise the fist action with a relaxed jaw. Keep the punch controlled rather than forceful.
Today, lift and lower the heels gently. Keep your balance and avoid hard landings.
Today, rehearse the complete Eight Brocades once. Give both bow directions the same controlled attention.
Today, notice your breathing through each Brocade. Never hold the breath to match a movement.
Today, explore controlled stance work. A smooth rise matters more than extra depth.
Today, stay with each Brocade a little longer in one sustained set. Keep a steady breath and controlled range rather than increasing speed.

days.title: Graduation · the full set and stillness

items.g: Today, bring the full set together and finish quietly. Notice steadiness, an easy breath and relaxed shoulders.

plans.title: Gentle Start Walk
plans.subtitle: 10 min · ease into movement
plans.description: An easy indoor walk — marching, heel pedals, step touches, side steps and rolling arms — finished with calf and shoulder stretches.

plans.title: Recovery Cool-Down
plans.subtitle: 10 min · stretch it out
plans.description: Slow marching into standing twists, side bends and long leg and shoulder stretches, with a quiet breath to finish.

plans.title: Balance & Stability Walk
plans.subtitle: 12 min · Tai Chi steps
plans.description: Tai Chi stance and weight shifts, sitting steps, the forward walk, cat steps, walking backward and cloud steps, finished on one leg.

plans.title: Tai Chi Walking
plans.subtitle: 21 days · steps, balance & moving calm
plans.description: Learn to walk the Tai Chi way: rooted stance, sitting steps, the heel-first forward walk, cat steps, walking backward and cloud steps — then the stepping forms that use them. Every week ends with a longer walking flow and an easy recovery day.

items.g: Today, feel the supporting foot before shifting weight. Keep the upper body upright and unhurried.
Today, place each sitting step lightly before committing your weight. Practise both legs with the same care.
Today, set down the heel first in the forward walk. Transfer weight only after the foot is placed.
Today, keep cat steps small and quiet. Let the support leg carry you without leaning forward.
Today, check the space behind you before walking backward. Use short steps and place each foot deliberately.
Today, organise the sideways cloud step. Move the feet without crossing or rushing the weight shift.
Today is a lighter walk. Use higher stances, smaller steps and a comfortable breathing rhythm.
Today, connect Wild Horse to a controlled forward step. Let the waist guide the opening hands.
Today, brush and push after your foot is placed. Keep the front knee aligned with the toes.
Today, connect Repulse the Monkey to short backward steps. Keep the head level and the space behind clear.

days.title: Golden Rooster · balance on one leg

Today, practise forward and backward patterns together. Reset your footing between demonstrations when needed.
Today, slow the steps down without holding your breath. Keep the weight transfer clear and comfortable.
Today, settle the supporting leg for White Crane. Lift the arms without lifting the shoulders.
Today, keep both heel kicks low and controlled. Recover a stable stance before changing sides.
Today, choose a comfortable low stance and a smooth rise. Do not lower farther than you can return steadily.
Today, carry a steady rhythm through one forward-focused flow. Place each step before moving the hands onward.
Today, prioritise balance through cloud steps and kicks. Pause to regain steadiness rather than rushing.
Today, practise an unhurried mindful walk. Notice the feet accepting weight with each small step.
Today, bring the walking skills and forms together once. Keep your range controlled and reset when necessary.

plans.subtitle: 15 min · arms up, heart up
plans.description: A brisk indoor walk with arms-up side taps, high-knee side taps, overhead hooks, high knees and a grapevine, cooled down with standing stretches.

plans.title: 30-Day Weight Loss Walking
plans.subtitle: 30 days · indoor walks from 11 to 15 minutes
plans.description: Indoor walking workouts with a new focus every day — arms-up cardio, knee drive, side steps, cross-body core, intervals and steady endurance, with dance-style side taps and cross-back steps. Every move is done once, and the work intervals grow longer each week, with an easy recovery walk every seventh day.

plans.title: Fat-Burn Intervals
plans.subtitle: 20 min · the longest indoor walk
plans.description: High knees and hamstring-curl combos alternate with easier steps for twenty minutes of low-impact intervals, then a full stretch.

plans.title: Gentle Flexibility Flow
plans.subtitle: 10 min · seated stretch
plans.description: Seated waist circles, shoulder rolls, cat-cow, side bends, a spinal twist, a chest opener and hamstring stretches from your chair.

plans.title: Neck & Shoulder Release
plans.subtitle: 10 min · seated relief
plans.description: Slow neck movements in every direction, shoulder rolls and extensions, and a chest opener to undo screen posture.

plans.title: Chair Qigong
plans.subtitle: 14 min · seated energy flow
plans.description: Seated breathing and the opening form, then chest openings, Lifting the Qi, Phoenix Wings, the rainbow, Catch the Moon and Washing the Face with Qi, all from your chair.

Today, gather and lower the arms gently. Choose an overhead range that feels comfortable.

Today, open the chest without arching the lower back. Keep your ribs comfortably over the pelvis.
Today, paint the rainbow with a relaxed side reach. Keep both sitting bones supported.

days.title: Waving Your Hands to the Sea

Today, make the Qi pulse small and smooth. Avoid tensing the wrists or holding your breath.
Today, rehearse the first ten seated forms once. Keep the hand paths connected at an unhurried pace.
Today, free the shoulders through one slower flow. Use a smaller range wherever you feel tension.
Today, soften the effort and pause in stillness. Let the hands settle without forcing a breathing count.
Today, lift the Qi with light hands. Keep the neck long and stop below any uncomfortable height.
Today, spread Phoenix Wings without shrugging. Keep your chest open and your elbows soft.
Today, gather the moon with rounded arms. Use a gentle torso turn rather than reaching too far.
Today, bring the hands towards the face softly. Keep the wrists loose and the shoulders quiet.
Today, explore a small spinal turn through one slower flow. Stay supported rather than leaning off the chair.
Today, rehearse all fourteen seated forms once. Keep each arm path smooth and leave time to reset.
Today, release the neck and shoulders. Keep head movements small and stop if they feel uncomfortable.
Today, move the arms like water through one continuous practice. Let the shoulders stay heavy and relaxed.
Today, connect the chest opening, rainbow and Qi lift. Keep the breath natural as the arm paths change.
Today, notice how opening and gathering balance each other. Finish each arm path before starting the next.
Today, notice the breath throughout the full seated flow. Never hold or lengthen it to force a match.
Today, keep the hips supported while the spine turns gently. Use one controlled pass of the forms.
Today, practise softly and finish in stillness. Let the face and jaw relax as the arms lower.
Today, bring all fourteen forms together once. Notice a steadier rhythm rather than chasing a larger range.

plans.subtitle: 12 min · tone from your seat
plans.description: Seated marching, rows, curls, knee extensions, hip openers and shoulder work for real strength without standing.

script.text: Welcome to your evening wind-down. Lie down comfortably, and let your eyes close whenever you're ready.
This is the end of your day. There is nothing left to do, and nowhere else to be.
Take a slow breath in through your nose… and let it go with a long, gentle sigh.
Once more. Breathe in… and breathe all the way out.
Now let your breathing find its own easy rhythm. There's no need to control it.
Picture today as a bag you have been carrying since the morning.
Imagine setting it down beside the bed. You can pick it up tomorrow, if you need it.
Notice the places where your body touches the bed. Your head, your back, your legs.
Let the bed hold all of your weight. You don't have to hold yourself up any more.
Soften your forehead. Let the space between your eyebrows grow wide and smooth.
Unclench your jaw. Let your tongue rest gently, and your lips part slightly.
Let your shoulders sink down, away from your ears, a little more with each breath out.
Feel your arms grow heavy, all the way down to your fingertips.
Let your belly rise and fall on its own, soft and warm, like a sleeping child's.
Let your hips release, and your legs grow heavy and still.
Feel your feet. Let every toe relax completely.
If a thought about today appears, simply notice it, and let it drift away like a leaf on a stream.
Now let's count ten slow breaths together, backwards, from ten to one.
Ten.
Nine.
Eight.
Seven.
Six.
Five.
Four.
Three.
Two.
One.
If you lost count along the way, that's perfectly fine. It means you're letting go.
Rest now in this quiet. Your body knows exactly how to sleep.
Stay here as long as you like. Let sleep come in its own time.
Goodnight.
Welcome. Lie on your back or on your side, whichever feels most like sleep to you.
Let your eyes close. We'll move slowly through the body, letting each part fall asleep before the next.
Take a slow breath in… and a long breath out, like a sigh at the end of a long day.
Once more… in… and out. Let the bed take all of your weight.
Bring your attention to the top of your head. Imagine a warm, soft light resting there.
Let that warmth melt across your scalp, loosening any tightness.
Your forehead softens and smooths. The tiny muscles around your eyes let go.
Your eyelids are heavy. Your eyes sink gently back and rest.
Your cheeks relax. Your jaw drops a little. Your tongue lies soft in your mouth.
The warmth flows down into your neck. The front of your throat and the back of your neck both soften.
Your shoulders melt down into the bed, wide and heavy.
Feel the warmth travel down your upper arms… your elbows… your forearms.
Your hands grow heavy. Each finger, one by one, completely relaxed.
Now your chest. Notice it rising and falling, slowly, without any effort.
Your upper back sinks into the mattress. Your spine lengthens and rests.
Let the warmth gather in your belly. Soft belly. Easy breath.
Your lower back releases. Feel it settle down into the bed.
Your hips grow heavy, sinking down, as if into warm sand.
The warmth flows into your thighs. Big, strong muscles, letting go completely.
Your knees soften. Your calves loosen and grow warm.
Your ankles relax. Your feet feel heavy and warm.
And finally your toes. Every single toe, still and at rest.
Now feel your whole body at once, from the top of your head to the tips of your toes.
One warm, heavy, peaceful body, resting completely.
If any spot still holds tension, breathe into it, and let the next breath out melt it away.
With each breath, you sink a little deeper into the bed, and a little deeper into rest.
Your body has done so much for you today. Now it can rest.
Let your breathing slow… and let your thoughts slow down with it.
There is nothing left to do. Your body is ready for sleep.
Let yourself drift now, softly, into deep and peaceful sleep.
Goodnight.
Welcome. Settle into bed, and let your body sink into the mattress.
Close your eyes. Tonight, we'll take a slow, quiet journey to a moonlit lake.
Begin with a deep breath in… and a long, slow breath out.
Again. In through the nose… and out, letting your whole body grow heavier.
Let your breathing slow down on its own, each breath a little softer than the last.
Imagine it's a warm summer night. You're walking along a soft path through tall pine trees.
The air is cool and fresh. It smells of pine, of earth, and of night flowers.
Your feet are bare. The ground beneath them is soft, mossy and warm.
Through the trees, you see a silver light shimmering ahead.
The path opens onto the shore of a wide, still lake, glowing under a full moon.
The water is perfectly calm. The moon rests on its surface like a silver coin.
Near the shore, a small wooden boat waits for you, lined with soft blankets.
You step in and lie down. The blankets are warm, and the boat rocks gently.
Slowly, the boat drifts away from the shore, carried by the stillest current.
Above you, the sky is filled with stars, more than you have ever seen.
With every breath, the boat rocks softly… up… and down… like a cradle.
Feel the warmth of the blankets around your shoulders, your arms, your legs.
Listen to the faint lapping of water against the wooden boat.
Any thoughts left from the day are like ripples. They spread out, and fade into stillness.
Your body is heavy and warm. Your mind is quiet and slow.
The moonlight washes over you, soft and silver, from your head down to your toes.
Each breath out carries you further across the water, into deeper calm.
There is nothing to do here. Nothing to remember. Only the gentle drift.
The lake holds you. The night holds you. You are completely safe.
Let your breathing become slow and deep, the breathing of sleep.
Drifting… softly… deeper… and deeper.
The stars blur gently as your eyes grow heavier behind closed lids.
Let go of the last thread of thought. Let the water carry you.
Stay in your little boat as long as you like, floating on the silver lake.
Let sleep come to you, as gently as moonlight.
Goodnight.
Welcome to Ocean Calm. Find a comfortable seat, or lie down, and let your eyes close.
Take a moment to arrive. Let your shoulders drop, and your hands rest.
Breathe in slowly through your nose… and breathe out through your mouth, long and slow.
Again. Breathe in… and let it go.
Now imagine you're sitting on a quiet beach in the early evening. The sand is warm beneath you.
In front of you, the ocean stretches all the way to the horizon, calm and blue.
Watch the waves roll in toward the shore… and slowly draw back out to sea.
Let your breath follow them. As a wave rolls in, breathe in.
As it slides back out, breathe out, long and slow.
In… with the wave. Out… with the wave.
There's no hurry. The ocean has been breathing like this for millions of years.
Feel the cool, salty breeze on your face, and the warmth of the sand beneath you.
Now, with each wave that leaves, imagine it taking one worry with it.
Let the water carry it away, further and further, until it disappears into the sea.
Another wave rolls in, bringing fresh, clean calm.
Another wave draws out, carrying away the tension from your shoulders and your jaw.
Rest in this steady rhythm. In… and out. Arriving… and leaving.
Notice how much lighter your body feels now, and how much slower your breathing has become.
This ocean is always here inside you. Whenever life feels rough, you can return to its rhythm.
Rest here a little longer, breathing with the waves.
Now let your breath return to its own natural rhythm.
Feel the surface beneath you, and the room around you.
When you're ready, gently open your eyes, and bring this calm with you.
Welcome. Sit comfortably, and let your hands rest wherever they feel easy.
Close your eyes, or let your gaze rest softly on the floor in front of you.
Let's begin with a calming sigh. Breathe in through your nose… take in a little more… and let it out slowly through your mouth.
Again. In… a little more… and let it all go.
One last time. In… top it up… and sigh it out.
Notice how your body feels now. Even a little softer counts.
Where are you holding today's stress? Your jaw? Your shoulders? Your stomach?
Just notice it, without judging. It's simply your body trying to protect you.
Now imagine you're sitting in a quiet bamboo grove. Tall green stalks sway gently all around you.
Listen to the leaves whispering as a soft breeze moves through the grove.
When the wind blows, the bamboo bends. It doesn't fight, and it doesn't break.
Let your body be like the bamboo. Rooted below, flexible above.
Breathe into the place where stress lives. Imagine your breath as warm sunlight reaching it.
With each breath out, let that tightness melt, like ice softening in the sun.
Soft jaw. Soft shoulders. Soft belly.
You don't have to fix anything right now. You're allowed to simply breathe.
The breeze comes and goes, just like your thoughts. Let them pass through.
Feel the calm that was underneath the stress all along.
Take a deep, slow breath in… and let it out gently.
Slowly bring your attention back to the room around you.
When you're ready, open your eyes. Carry the softness of the bamboo with you.
Welcome. Sit comfortably, and rest one or both hands over the centre of your chest.
Close your eyes, and feel the warmth of your hands, and the gentle rise and fall beneath them.
Breathe in slowly… and breathe out, letting the area around your heart soften.
Think of a moment when someone was truly kind to you. Let yourself feel it again.
Notice the warmth that memory brings. Let it spread through your chest.
Now offer that same kindness to yourself. Silently repeat after me.
May I be safe.
May I be healthy.
May I be peaceful.
May I live with ease.
If this feels awkward, that's alright. Kindness is something we practise, like any skill.
Now bring to mind someone you love easily. See their face, their smile.
Wish them well. May you be safe. May you be healthy.
May you be peaceful. May you live with ease.
Feel how naturally the warmth flows toward them.
Now picture someone you see often but barely know. A neighbour, a shopkeeper, a colleague.
They want to be happy too, just like you. Offer them the same wishes.
May you be safe. May you be healthy. May you be peaceful. May you live with ease.
If you wish, bring to mind someone you find a little difficult. Start with someone easy to forgive.
Without excusing anything, simply wish them peace. May you be free from suffering.
Notice what happens in your heart. Whatever you feel is okay.
Now let your kindness spread wider, like ripples on water. To your town, your country, the whole world.
May all beings be safe. May all beings be healthy.
May all beings be peaceful. May all beings live with ease.
Finally, return to yourself. Feel your hands resting on your heart.
May I be kind to myself today.
Take a deep breath in… and gently let it go.
When you're ready, open your eyes, and carry this warmth into your day.
Welcome. In this practice, we'll gently tense and release the body, one area at a time.
Sit or lie down comfortably, and let your eyes close. Imagine soft rain falling outside your window.
Take a deep breath in… and let it out slowly, like rain sliding down glass.
Use only about half your strength when you tense. Never strain, and skip any area that hurts.
Let's begin with your hands. Make two gentle fists… squeeze… and hold.
And release. Let your fingers uncurl, and feel the warmth flow in.
Now your arms. Bend your elbows and gently tighten your arms… hold.
And let go. Let your arms fall heavy and loose.
Lift your shoulders up toward your ears… squeeze them up… hold.
And drop them. Feel the tension slide away, like water running off a roof.
Now your face. Scrunch your eyes, your nose and your mouth together… hold.
And release. Let your whole face go smooth and soft.
Clench your jaw lightly, pressing your tongue to the roof of your mouth… hold.
And let go. Let your jaw hang loose, with your lips slightly apart.
Now your belly. Draw it in toward your spine and tighten it gently… hold.
And release. Let your belly go soft and round, rising with each breath.
Press your knees together and tighten your legs… hold.
And let go. Feel your legs melt down, heavy and warm.
Finally, curl your toes and tighten your feet… hold.
And release. Let your feet go completely limp.
Now rest. Listen to the soft rain in your mind, steady and gentle.
Let it wash over your whole body, rinsing away any tension that remains.
Scan from head to toe. If you find any tightness, breathe into it, and let it soften.
Notice the difference between tension and release. This softness is always available to you.
Rest in this rain-soaked stillness. Heavy, warm and calm.
Each drop of rain is a quiet reminder. Let go… let go… let go.
Your body feels loose and light. Your breath is slow and easy.
Begin to deepen your breath a little. Wiggle your fingers and your toes.
Gently stretch in any way that feels good.
When you're ready, open your eyes. Take this stillness with you into your day.
Welcome to box breathing, a simple technique to calm the body and steady the mind.
Sit tall but relaxed, with your feet flat on the floor and your hands resting in your lap.
We'll breathe in a square. In for four, hold for four, out for four, and hold for four.
Breathe through your nose, and keep every count smooth and gentle. Never force it.
Follow the circle and my voice. First, breathe all the way out.
Now let your breath be natural for a moment. Notice how you feel.
Good. Let's do another round. Breathe all the way out… and begin.
Release the pattern, and let your breathing return to its own rhythm.
Well done. Use box breathing any time you need to feel calm and steady.
Welcome to 4-7-8 breathing, a slow, soothing pattern that helps the body unwind.
Sit comfortably with your back straight, or lie down if you're getting ready for sleep.
Rest the tip of your tongue just behind your upper front teeth, and keep it there throughout.
Breathe in quietly through your nose for four. Hold for seven. Then breathe out through your mouth for eight, with a soft whoosh.
If the counts feel long, simply count a little faster. The long, slow breath out is what matters.
Breathe out completely through your mouth… and let's begin.
Let your breathing return to normal. Notice any heaviness or warmth in your body.
If you felt a little light-headed, that's common at first. Breathe naturally until it passes.
When you're ready, breathe out fully… and we'll do one more round.
Release the counting, and let your breath flow on its own.
Notice how calm and settled you feel.
Practise this twice a day, and it becomes easier and more soothing over time.
Welcome to the Qigong Breath of Energy. Stand with soft knees, or sit near the front of your chair.
Rest both hands on your lower belly, just below your navel. In Qigong, this is the dantian, your energy centre.
Relax your shoulders, tuck your chin slightly, and imagine a thread lifting the crown of your head.
We'll breathe in for four, pause for two, and breathe out slowly for six, all through the nose.
As you breathe in, let your belly expand into your hands. As you breathe out, let it gently draw back.
Begin by breathing out completely.
Breathe naturally now. Feel the warmth gathering beneath your hands.
This time, as you breathe in, imagine fresh, bright energy rising from the earth into your belly.
As you breathe out, let tiredness and heaviness flow down and out through your feet.
Breathe out completely… and begin.
Rest, breathing naturally. Notice any tingling, warmth or lightness in your hands and body.
One final round. Breathe in vitality… breathe out anything you no longer need.
Let your breath return to normal, with your hands resting on your belly.
Your energy is gathered and ready. Enjoy the rest of your day.
Good morning. Find a comfortable seat, and let your spine grow tall and easy.
Close your eyes for a moment. Before the day begins, this time is just for you.
Take a deep breath in, filling your lungs from the bottom up… and breathe out slowly.
Again. Breathe in the fresh morning air… and let any sleepiness drift out with the breath.
Now let your breathing settle into an easy, natural rhythm.
Notice how your body feels this morning. Rested or tired, light or heavy. Just notice.
Gently roll your shoulders once or twice, and let them settle down.
Imagine soft morning light shining on your face, warm and golden.
Let it spread through your whole body, gently waking up every part of you.
Now think about the day ahead. Not your to-do list, but how you'd like to feel.
Maybe calm. Maybe focused. Maybe kind, or patient, or brave.
Choose one word for today, and let it settle into your mind.
Breathe in, and silently say your word. Breathe out, and feel it in your body.
Imagine moving through your day with this quality. Meeting people and facing challenges, all with this word.
Whatever happens today, you can come back to this word, and to this breath.
Take one more deep, energising breath in… hold it for a moment at the top… and let it go.
Wiggle your fingers and toes. Feel the energy in your hands.
Open your eyes, and step into your day with clarity.
Good morning, and welcome to Gratitude Sunrise. Sit comfortably, and let your eyes close.
Take a slow breath in… and a long, easy breath out. Let yourself arrive.
Once more. Breathe in… and breathe out, letting your shoulders soften.
Imagine you're sitting on a hillside just before dawn. The sky is turning pale blue and gold.
As you watch, the very edge of the sun appears on the horizon.
Feel its first warm light touch your face. A brand-new day is beginning.
Now bring to mind something simple you're grateful for. Perhaps a warm drink, or a comfortable bed.
Let yourself really feel it. Notice where gratitude lives in your body.
Now think of a person you're grateful for. See their face in the morning light.
Silently thank them, and notice the warmth that rises in your chest.
Bring to mind something your body did for you yesterday. Walking, breathing, healing, resting.
Thank your body. It works for you every moment, even now.
Think of a small moment from the past week that made you smile.
Let that smile return to your face, just a little.
As the sun rises higher, let its light fill you with these grateful feelings.
Breathe in warmth and gratitude… breathe out, and let it spread through your whole body.
Rest here, in the glow of a full heart.
Gratitude doesn't change what happens today. It changes how you meet it.
Now set a small intention: to notice one more thing to be thankful for, later today.
Feel the sun now fully risen, warm and bright above the hills.
Take a deep breath in… and let it out with a gentle smile.
Begin to move your fingers and toes, and feel the room around you.
When you're ready, open your eyes, and begin your day with a full heart.
Welcome. Sit upright and relaxed, like a mountain beside a quiet lake.
Let your eyes close, or rest your gaze softly on a point in front of you.
Take three slow breaths with me. In… and out.
In… and out.
In… and out. Now let your breath find its own pace.
Imagine a glass of muddy water. When you stop shaking it, the mud slowly settles, and the water becomes clear.
Your mind works the same way. We don't force it to be calm. We simply stop stirring it.
Bring your attention to the feeling of breath at the tip of your nose. Cool air in, warm air out.
Now we'll count breaths. Count one as you breathe out, two on the next breath out, up to ten.
If you lose count or drift into a thought, smile, and start again at one.
Each time you return is a moment of training. There is no failure here.
Keep counting softly. One… two… three…
If sounds arise, let them be part of the lake's surface. They come, and they go.
Notice the space between your thoughts. Rest in that clear, quiet space.
Your attention is becoming steadier, like water settling.
Now let go of counting, and simply rest with the breath.
Clear. Calm. Present.
Slowly widen your awareness. Notice your body, your seat, the room around you.
Take a deeper breath in… and let it go.
Open your eyes, and carry this clarity into your next task.
Welcome to Mindful Walking. Find a quiet space where you can walk ten or fifteen steps in a line.
Keep your eyes open, with your gaze soft and resting on the ground a few steps ahead.
Stand still for a moment. Feel your feet on the ground, and your weight balanced between them.
Let your knees be soft, your shoulders relaxed, and your arms hanging easily.
Take a deep breath in… and let it out.
Now slowly shift your weight onto your left foot. Notice your right foot becoming light.
Lift your right foot, move it forward, and place it down, heel first, then toes.
Feel your weight roll forward onto it. Now the left foot becomes light.
Continue walking at half your usual speed, or slower. Lifting… moving… placing.
Notice every part of the step. The lift, the swing, the touch, the shift of weight.
If your mind wanders, pause for a moment. Feel your feet. Then continue.
When you reach the end of your path, stop and stand still. Then turn around slowly, with full attention.
Now let your breath join your steps. Breathe in for one step… and breathe out for the next.
Feel the ground supporting you with every step. Steady. Rooted. Like a tree that can walk.
Notice the air on your skin, the sounds around you, the light in front of you.
There's nowhere to get to. Each step is the destination.
Let your walking become smooth and continuous, like the slow flow of Tai Chi.
If you like, walk even slower now. Feel how much balance each step needs.
Every step is a chance to come back to the present moment.
Slowly come to a stop. Stand still, with both feet on the ground.
Feel your whole body standing here, alive and present.
Take a deep breath in… and let it out.
Carry this steady, mindful presence with you into every step today.

meditations.title: Mindful Listening
meditations.subtitle: Let the music anchor your mind

script.text: Welcome to Mindful Listening. Sit comfortably, and let your eyes gently close.
In this practice, sound will be your anchor. There's nothing to think about. Only listening.
Take a slow breath in… and let it out.
Now bring your attention to the music around you. Simply listen.
Notice a single note. Hear where it begins… how it lingers… and how it fades away.
Follow the next note in the same way. Beginning… lingering… fading.
When your mind drifts into thinking, that's natural. Gently come back to the next sound you hear.
Now notice the quiet spaces between the notes. Let your attention rest there too.
That silence is not empty. It's spacious, peaceful and alive.
Let the sounds move through you, like a breeze through an open window.
Now widen your listening. Notice sounds beyond the music. The room. The world outside.
No sound is good or bad. Each one simply arises, and passes.
You don't need to name them or follow them. Just receive them.
Notice the one who is listening. Calm, aware, and still.
Rest here, in open listening.
Each sound is born and fades, just like every thought and every feeling.
Let the music carry you into deeper stillness.
Now gently bring your attention back to your breath.
Notice your body sitting here, and the space around you.
Take a full, deep breath in… and let it go.
When you're ready, open your eyes, and keep listening to the world with this same calm attention.
Welcome to the Full Body Scan. Lie down on your back, or sit comfortably in a chair.
Let your eyes close. In this practice, we simply notice the body, with curiosity and kindness.
There's no right way to feel. Warmth, coolness, tingling, or nothing at all. Everything is welcome.
Take a slow breath in… and a long breath out. Feel the weight of your body resting.
Bring your attention down to your left foot. Notice your toes, the sole of your foot, the heel.
What sensations are here? Pressure, temperature, the touch of a sock or the air.
Now let your attention move up into your left ankle, your shin and calf, and your knee.
Move up through your left thigh to your hip. Notice where your body meets the floor or the chair.
Now shift your attention to your right foot. Your toes… the sole… the heel.
Move up through the right ankle, the shin and calf, and the knee.
Continue up through your right thigh to your right hip.
Notice both legs together now. Resting. Supported.
Bring your awareness to your pelvis and lower back. Notice any tightness, and simply breathe with it.
Move up to your belly. Feel it rise as you breathe in… and fall as you breathe out.
Notice your chest. Your ribs expanding and softening with every breath.
Now your upper back and shoulder blades. Let them rest heavily.
Bring your attention to both shoulders. If you find tension, imagine breathing right into it.
Move down both arms, through your elbows and forearms, to your wrists.
Notice your hands. The palms, the backs of the hands, each finger. Perhaps a gentle tingling.
Now the neck. The front of the throat, the sides, the back of the neck.
Notice your jaw, and let it soften. Notice your lips, your tongue, your cheeks.
Your nose, and the breath moving through it. Your eyes, resting behind closed lids.
Your forehead, your temples, your ears, the back of your head.
And finally, the very top of your head.
Now expand your awareness to hold your whole body at once, as one living, breathing whole.
Feel the breath moving through the entire body, from head to toe, and from toe to head.
Rest in this awareness. Simply being here, in your body, just as it is.
Your body is always in the present moment. You can return to it whenever your mind is busy.
Begin to deepen your breath now. Gently move your fingers and toes.
Stretch in any way that feels good, and notice how your body feels after this practice.
Take one last deep breath in… and let it go.
When you're ready, open your eyes, feeling awake, aware and refreshed.

guides.title: The 5 principles of Tai Chi
guides.subtitle: What makes slow movement so powerful
guides.intro: Tai Chi looks simple from the outside — soft arms, slow steps, a calm face. Underneath, five quiet principles turn those movements into training for balance, strength and a settled mind.

sections.heading: 1 · Relax, don't collapse
sections.body: Song, the Chinese word for relaxed, means releasing tension you don't need while keeping the posture you do. Shoulders drop, the jaw softens, but the spine stays long. You'll feel it most in the hands: alive, never limp.

sections.heading: 2 · Root through your feet
sections.body: Imagine your weight sinking into the floor through the soles of your feet. A slight bend in the knees lets the legs do the work, which builds strength in the ankles, knees and hips — the very joints that keep us steady.

sections.heading: 3 · Move from the centre
sections.body: Every arm movement begins a moment earlier in the waist. Turning from the centre protects the lower back and links the whole body into one smooth, efficient motion.

sections.heading: 4 · Separate full and empty
sections.body: At any moment one leg carries more weight than the other. Shifting it slowly and completely is the heart of balance training — your body learns exactly where its centre is.

sections.heading: 5 · Let the breath lead
sections.body: Breathing low into the belly, in through the nose, lets the pace of the movement follow the pace of the breath. Slower breath, calmer nervous system, softer movement.

guides.title: Why slow movement builds balance
guides.subtitle: The quiet training your body loves
guides.intro: Balance isn't a fixed trait — it's a skill your brain and body practise together. Slow, deliberate movement happens to be one of the best ways to train it.

sections.heading: Your three balance sensors
sections.body: Your eyes, your inner ear and thousands of tiny sensors in your feet and joints all report where you are in space. Moving slowly gives each of them time to talk to your brain, so the whole system gets sharper.

sections.heading: Strength where it counts
sections.body: Holding a soft knee bend while shifting weight works the muscles around your ankles, knees and hips in long, gentle bursts — exactly the strength that helps you recover when you trip.

sections.heading: Confidence is part of it
sections.body: When moving feels safe and controlled, you move more. That alone keeps joints supple and muscles engaged, creating a positive loop that compounds week after week.

takeaways: Balance is trainable at any age

guides.title: Breathing 101
guides.subtitle: Three breaths to calm you in a minute
guides.intro: The breath is the only part of the nervous system you can steer on purpose. A longer exhale is a direct signal to your body that it's safe to slow down.

sections.heading: Belly breath
sections.body: Rest a hand on your belly. Breathe in through the nose and let the hand rise; breathe out and let it fall. Five slow rounds are enough to notice a shift.

sections.heading: Box breath · 4-4-4-4
sections.body: Inhale for four, hold for four, exhale for four, hold for four. The steady rhythm gives a busy mind something simple to follow. Great before a meeting or a hard conversation.

sections.heading: 4-7-8 for sleep
sections.body: Inhale quietly for four, hold for seven, and exhale slowly through the mouth for eight. Start with four rounds. If holding feels uncomfortable, shorten every count — the long exhale is what matters.

guides.title: Chair practice, done right
guides.subtitle: Set up for safe, strong seated sessions
guides.intro: A chair turns every session into a supported one — perfect for stiff joints, busy days or rebuilding confidence. A few details make it even better.

sections.heading: Pick the right chair
sections.body: Choose a sturdy chair without wheels or arms, on a non-slip floor. Your feet should rest flat with knees roughly level with your hips.

sections.heading: Sit on the front half
sections.body: Scoot forward so your back is free and your spine can lengthen. Imagine a thread lifting the crown of your head while your sit bones sink down.

sections.heading: Use it as a partner
sections.body: Holding the seat for twists and leg lifts adds stability. For standing moves, keep the chair in front of you as a steady hand-rail.

guides.title: Qi, explained simply
guides.subtitle: An old idea with a modern feel
guides.intro: Qi (pronounced chee) is often translated as energy or vitality. You don't need to believe anything mystical to benefit — think of it as the feeling of a body that's warm, loose and awake.

sections.heading: What practitioners notice
sections.body: Warmth or tingling in the hands, a looser back, deeper breaths, a quieter mind. These are the everyday signs of circulation, relaxed muscles and a calmer nervous system.

sections.heading: Why the movements repeat
sections.body: Qigong forms repeat a single gentle movement many times, in rhythm with the breath. Repetition lets you stop thinking and start feeling — which is where the calm comes from.

sections.heading: How to practise
sections.body: Stand or sit comfortably, soften your knees, and follow the breath. Small and smooth beats big and forced. Finish by resting your hands on your lower belly for three breaths.

guides.title: Build a 10-minute habit
guides.subtitle: Make practice the easiest part of your day
guides.intro: Motivation fades; habits stay. The trick is to make your practice so small and so linked to your day that skipping it feels stranger than doing it.

sections.heading: Anchor it
sections.body: Attach practice to something you already do — after your morning tea, before your lunch break, when you brush your teeth at night. Set your TaiChi Flow reminder for that moment.

sections.heading: Shrink it on hard days
sections.body: On busy or low-energy days, do just one movement or a two-minute breath. Keeping the streak alive matters more than the length of the session.

sections.heading: Notice the payoff
sections.body: After each session, take one breath and notice how you feel. Linking the practice to a good feeling is what makes the habit stick.

tips.title: Soft knees, strong legs
tips.body: Keep a gentle bend in your knees in every standing move. It protects the joints and quietly builds leg strength.

tips.title: Exhale a little longer
tips.body: Make each out-breath one count longer than the in-breath. It's the quickest way to tell your body it can relax.

tips.title: Move at the speed of breath
tips.body: If you're rushing, you've left your breath behind. Slow the movement until the two feel connected again.

tips.title: Small is still practice
tips.body: Two minutes of mindful movement on a busy day keeps the habit alive. Consistency beats intensity.

tips.title: Let the shoulders drop
tips.body: Check in now: are your shoulders near your ears? Breathe out and let them melt down your back.

tips.title: Root through all four corners
tips.body: Feel the big toe, little toe and both sides of the heel pressing evenly. Balance starts at the feet.

tips.title: Turn from the waist
tips.body: Let your arms follow your centre, not lead it. Turning from the waist keeps the lower back happy.

tips.title: Water first
tips.body: Sip a glass of water before your session. Even mild dehydration can make muscles feel tight and tired.

tips.title: Same time, same cue
tips.body: Link practice to something you already do daily — morning tea or brushing your teeth — and it becomes automatic.

tips.title: Notice, then move
tips.body: Take three breaths before you begin and simply notice how your body feels. You'll move more kindly.

tips.title: Chair as a partner
tips.body: Hold the back of a sturdy chair for any balance move. Support isn't cheating — it's how confidence grows.

tips.title: Soft gaze, steady body
tips.body: Rest your eyes on a still point ahead during balance work. A steady gaze helps a steady body.

tips.title: Warm hands, calm mind
tips.body: Rub your palms together until warm, then rest them over your eyes for three breaths. Instant reset.

tips.title: Range before reach
tips.body: Move only as far as feels smooth. Range grows naturally when the body feels safe.

tips.title: Breathe low
tips.body: Place a hand on your belly and breathe so it rises first. Low breathing is calmer breathing.

tips.title: Evening wind-down
tips.body: A slow five-minute flow before bed tells your nervous system the day is done. Try it tonight.

tips.title: Celebrate the streak
tips.body: Every session counts, however short. Notice the streak and give yourself credit — it fuels tomorrow.

tips.title: Tension check
tips.body: Unclench your jaw, soften your tongue from the roof of your mouth, relax your brow. Feel the difference?

tips.title: Walk mindfully
tips.body: On your next walk, match four steps to an in-breath and four to an out-breath. Moving meditation.

tips.title: Sit tall, not stiff
tips.body: Imagine a thread lifting the crown of your head. Length in the spine, softness everywhere else.

tips.title: Shake it out
tips.body: Thirty seconds of loose shaking through hands, arms and legs releases stiffness after sitting.

tips.title: Morning light
tips.body: Practise near a window in the morning. Daylight helps set your body clock for better sleep tonight.

tips.title: Kind effort
tips.body: Aim for about 60% effort. Tai Chi rewards ease — strain closes the body, softness opens it.

tips.title: Listen to your body
tips.body: Discomfort that feels sharp or pinching is a stop sign. Ease off, adjust, or choose the seated version.

tips.title: One breath reset
tips.body: Stressed? Inhale for four, pause, exhale for six. One breath can change the next ten minutes.

tips.title: Ankles matter
tips.body: Draw slow circles with each ankle while you wait for the kettle. Strong, mobile ankles prevent wobbles.

tips.title: Finish with stillness
tips.body: End each session with hands resting on your lower belly for three breaths. Let the benefits settle.

tips.title: Progress, not perfection
tips.body: Your form will never be perfect — nobody's is. Every repetition teaches your body something new.

tips.title: Sleep is training
tips.body: Muscles and balance improve while you rest. A regular bedtime makes your practice work harder for you.

tips.title: Share the calm
tips.body: Invite a friend or family member to practise with you. Calm is contagious — and so is consistency.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: TaiChi Flow is a guided Tai Chi, Qigong, chair exercise, walking and meditation app. This policy explains what happens to your information when you use it. The short version: your answers, health details and practice history stay on your phone; a small set of app events is shared for ad measurement only when your privacy choice allows it; purchases are handled by Apple or Google with RevenueCat.

sections.h: Information that stays on your device
p: Your onboarding answers (such as age range, goals, body measurements, activity level, comfort with balance or mobility, and any areas you want to protect), your plan, practice history, favourites, reminders and settings are stored only on your phone. TaiChi Flow has no accounts and does not upload this information automatically.
You can erase it at any time in Profile → Reset all data, or by uninstalling the app.

When you use Tell us what you need, we store your message, optional reply email, submission time, app version and platform in a private inbox hosted by Lovable Cloud. Other app users cannot read these messages. No onboarding answers, practice history, purchase identifier or advertising identifier is attached. Please do not include health or payment details.

We use these messages to respond to requests and improve the app, not for advertising. Our hosting provider also processes technical connection information to deliver the request. To request access or deletion, email pranacodes@gmail.com and identify your message.
We retain messages only as long as needed to handle the request and related follow-up. Resetting the app does not delete a message you have already sent.
Payments are processed by the Apple App Store or Google Play under their own terms. We never see your card or payment details.

We use RevenueCat to confirm purchases, unlock TaiChi Flow Plus and restore it on a new device. RevenueCat receives a random app user ID, your purchase and subscription history for this app, the store country and currency, and basic device and app information (model, operating system, app version, IP address). When your privacy choice allows ad measurement, it also receives the advertising identifier and Meta's anonymous app ID so renewals can be matched to our ads.

To understand which parts of the app help people and where they get stuck, the app can send usage events to PostHog (PostHog Inc., servers in the United States): screens opened, onboarding steps reached (not your answers), plans viewed or closed, the reason you pick when closing a plan screen, checkout started, purchases with their plan, price and currency, lessons and meditations started or finished with their length, and the star rating you give.

These events carry a random ID created on your phone, your app language, whether you have TaiChi Flow Plus, the app version, the operating system and your IP address. We never send your onboarding answers, health or mobility details, name or email, and never your advertising identifier.

Usage analytics follow the same privacy choice as ad measurement: in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, Switzerland and wherever your region cannot be determined, nothing is sent unless you choose Allow; elsewhere it is on by default and you can turn it off at any time in Profile → Privacy choices. PostHog processes this data under its own privacy policy (posthog.com/privacy).

We advertise TaiChi Flow on Facebook and Instagram. To learn which ads bring people to the app, the app can send these events to Meta: app installed or opened, onboarding finished, first session finished, plans viewed, checkout started, and trial, subscription or one-time purchases with their price and currency.

With these events Meta receives technical data such as device model, operating system, app version, IP address, Meta's anonymous app ID and — only where allowed — your device advertising identifier (IDFA on iPhone after you allow tracking; the Google advertising ID on Android). We never send your onboarding answers, health or mobility details, name, email or practice history.

In the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, Switzerland and wherever your region cannot be determined, nothing is sent unless you choose Allow in the privacy sheet. Elsewhere, measurement is on by default and you can turn it off at any time in Profile → Privacy choices. On iPhone, the advertising identifier is used only if you allow tracking when iOS asks.

Meta processes this data under its own Data Policy (facebook.com/privacy/policy). You can also limit ad tracking on your device: on iPhone in Settings → Privacy & Security → Tracking; on Android in Settings → Google → Ads (delete or reset the advertising ID).
Practice reminders are scheduled locally on your phone; no push service or notification token is used.

The first screens, onboarding audio and basic coaching sounds are included in the app. Lesson films, lesson voice, music, voice packs for other app languages and course updates are downloaded from our content storage (Cloudflare R2) when you open a lesson or when the app checks for updates, then kept on your phone so they play offline afterwards. Like any web server, the storage receives your IP address and basic request details to deliver the files; no account, advertising identifier, onboarding answer or practice history is sent with these downloads.

We process purchase information to provide the service you buy (contract), voluntarily submitted support messages to respond and improve our service (legitimate interests), and ad-measurement events and usage analytics where consent is required only on the basis of your consent, which you can withdraw at any time in Profile → Privacy choices. Withdrawing consent stops future sharing; it does not affect sharing that happened before.

Your practice history is stored on your phone, so you control it directly; only the usage events described above leave it. For information held by RevenueCat, PostHog or Meta about this app, you can ask us to access or delete it, or object to its use, by emailing us. Include the support code shown in Profile → Privacy choices if you can, so we can find the right records. You may also complain to your local data protection authority.

On-device data stays until you reset it or uninstall the app. Purchase records are kept by the stores and RevenueCat for as long as required for tax and accounting. Ad-measurement events are kept by Meta and usage analytics by PostHog according to their policies. Data shared with our providers travels over encrypted connections and may be processed outside your country under the providers' safeguards.
TaiChi Flow is made for adults. It is not directed to children under 16, and we do not knowingly collect information from them.
If we change what is shared or with whom, we will update this policy and ask for your choice again where consent is required.
Questions or requests: pranacodes@gmail.com.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: These terms apply when you download or use TaiChi Flow. By using the app you agree to them. If you downloaded the app from the Apple App Store, Apple's Standard Licensed Application End User License Agreement also applies.

p: TaiChi Flow offers general wellness guidance, not medical advice. Talk to your doctor before starting any new exercise programme, especially if you are pregnant, recovering from surgery or injury, or live with a heart, joint, balance or other medical condition.

Move within a comfortable range, use a chair or wall for support whenever you need it, and stop immediately if you feel pain, dizziness, shortness of breath or discomfort. You practise at your own risk.
Some courses and classes need TaiChi Flow Plus. Prices are shown in the app before you buy and are charged to your Apple ID or Google Play account.

Subscriptions renew automatically at the end of each period unless cancelled at least 24 hours before the period ends; your account is charged for the renewal within 24 hours before that. Where a free trial is offered, it converts to a paid subscription when the trial ends unless you cancel at least 24 hours before. Any unused part of a trial is forfeited when you buy a subscription.

You can manage or cancel subscriptions in your App Store or Google Play account settings. Deleting the app does not cancel a subscription. Lifetime access is a one-time purchase. Refunds are handled by Apple or Google under their policies.

We give you a personal, non-transferable licence to use the app and its content for your own practice. Please do not copy, resell, redistribute or reverse-engineer the app, its films, voice recordings or other content.
We keep improving courses and may add, change or retire content. We aim to keep the app available and accurate but provide it "as is", without warranties of any kind to the extent the law allows.

To the extent permitted by law, we are not liable for indirect or consequential losses, or for injury arising from exercises practised against this guidance. Nothing in these terms limits rights you have under consumer law that cannot be excluded.
We may update these terms; the date below shows the latest version. Continuing to use the app after an update means you accept the new terms.
Questions: pranacodes@gmail.com.
